data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Arri was a nymph, a goddess of the mountains and the wilderness. Her name is derived from the Greek word for mountain, 'arrhos'. She was often depicted as a beautiful and powerful figure, dressed in wildflowers and holding a staff or a pinecone. The name Arri carries the meaning “Mountain of god” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Arri usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
